CE1.label: Quick resolution — minimal effort

CE1.1.label: Immediate answer provided
CE1.1.description: Agent answered the customer's question directly and immediately. No investigation, escalation, or follow-up needed. Typically how-to questions or policy clarifications.

CE1.2.label: Simple lookup or verification
CE1.2.description: Agent performed a quick system lookup and resolved the issue (e.g. checked indexing status, verified citation data, confirmed coverage). Customer waited briefly but resolution was straightforward.

CE1.3.label: Self-service guidance successful
CE1.3.description: Agent pointed the customer to a self-service tool or process (e.g. Author Feedback Wizard, Scopus Source page) and the customer was able to resolve their issue independently.

CE1.description: Interactions resolved quickly with minimal customer effort. The customer's question or issue was addressed in a single contact with clear communication and no friction.

CE2.label: Process complexity & multi-step resolution

CE2.1.label: Customer required to provide extensive documentation
CE2.1.description: Customer had to gather and submit multiple pieces of information (DOIs, ISBNs, screenshots, spreadsheets of corrections) to get their issue resolved. The data collection burden fell on the customer.

CE2.2.label: Multi-step correction or verification process
CE2.2.description: Resolution required multiple sequential steps (e.g. verify article → submit correction → wait for editorial review → confirm fix). Each step added elapsed time and cognitive load.

CE2.3.label: Complex form or submission required
CE2.3.description: Customer had to navigate a complex form, application process, or structured submission (e.g. journal suggestion form, Author Feedback Wizard with many fields, CSAB application).

CE2.4.label: Policy or criteria explanation needed
CE2.4.description: Agent had to explain complex policies, evaluation criteria, or methodologies (e.g. CiteScore methodology, CSAB selection criteria, content policy). Customer effort came from understanding the complexity.

CE2.description: Effort driven by the inherent complexity of the resolution process — multiple steps required, detailed information needed from the customer, or complex verification procedures.

CE3.label: Wait time, delays & follow-up friction

CE3.1.label: Escalation to specialist team required
CE3.1.description: Issue needed to be escalated to a specialist team (editorial, content, technical) with a wait time. Customer had to wait for an internal process they couldn't see or influence.

CE3.2.label: Long wait for content update or correction
CE3.2.description: The resolution depends on a content update cycle (e.g. next CiteScore recalculation, monthly content load, quarterly re-evaluation). Customer has to wait for a scheduled batch process.

CE3.3.label: Follow-up required by customer
CE3.3.description: Customer had to proactively follow up to check status, remind the team, or ask for updates. Resolution was not proactively communicated.

CE3.4.label: Repeat contact about same issue
CE3.4.description: Customer is contacting support again about an issue they've raised before. Previous contact did not resolve it, or the resolution was incomplete or reverted.

CE3.description: Effort driven by waiting — for responses, escalation outcomes, content updates, or scheduled processes. The customer's issue was acknowledged but resolution was delayed.

CE4.label: Communication, transparency & handoff friction

CE4.1.label: Transferred between teams or agents
CE4.1.description: Customer was transferred to a different team, department, or agent during the interaction. Had to re-explain the issue or wait for a new agent to review the case.

CE4.2.label: Had to repeat issue or re-provide information
CE4.2.description: Customer had to explain their issue more than once — either because of a transfer, or because the agent didn't capture the details correctly the first time.

CE4.3.label: Unclear next steps or timeline
CE4.3.description: Agent did not clearly communicate what would happen next, when the customer could expect resolution, or what the customer needed to do. Left the customer in uncertainty.

CE4.4.label: Self-service option failed or was inadequate
CE4.4.description: Customer tried a self-service option (Author Feedback Wizard, Source suggestion form, FAQ) but it didn't work, was confusing, or didn't cover their case — forcing them to contact support.

CE4.5.label: Other communication or handoff friction
CE4.5.description: Communication issues not fitting above, including language barriers, inconsistent information from different agents, or lack of case history awareness.

CE4.description: Effort driven by poor communication — unclear explanations, being transferred between teams, having to repeat the issue, or lack of visibility into resolution progress.
